//: Security headers for the FRONTEND (the HTML the browser renders).
These have to live here rather than in helmet. The API and the static
frontend are two separate Vercel services, so a header set by Express
only ever lands on a JSON response — it never reaches the document the
browser is actually executing scripts in. Setting a strict CSP in
Express and assuming the SPA is protected is a silent no-op, which is
exactly why both halves are written down and cross-referenced.
The CSP directives, one at a time:
default-src 'self'      nothing loads from anywhere but our origin
script-src 'self'       no inline scripts, no CDNs. This is the
directive that actually stops XSS: an
injected <script> has no valid source.
style-src ... 'unsafe-inline'  a real, deliberate weakening. Recharts
(the dashboard charts) sets style attributes
at runtime, and CSP treats those as inline
styles. Removing it would need nonces on
every generated element, which a third-party
chart library does not offer. Inline STYLE is
a far smaller risk than inline SCRIPT — the
worst case is defacement, not code execution.
font-src / style-src google  the app loads IBM Plex Sans from Google
Fonts; these two hosts are what that needs.
img-src 'self' data:    data: covers inline SVG icons.
connect-src 'self'      XHR/fetch may only reach our own API, so an
injected script cannot exfiltrate data to an
attacker's server even if it runs.
frame-ancestors 'none'  nobody may frame the app — clickjacking.
object-src 'none'       no Flash/applet embeds, a legacy XSS vector.
form-action 'self'      a form cannot be repointed at another site.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'

headers.//: Deny browser features the app never uses, so an injected script cannot ask for them either.
